tier_reason: The README's Performance section has a first-party redis-benchmark table against Valkey 8.0.4 (10,000 requests per op), and the script is public (tests/performance/test_benchmark.sh, run via ./run_tests.sh perf). No CPU model, compiler or build flags are stated, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: Results are mixed. The single-command wins are small (0-8%; SADD is equal, INCR is +2%), PING pipelining is +25%, and Valkey is 94% faster on SET pipelining (588k vs 303k ops/s). Each op runs only 10,000 requests, with 10-command pipelines. The baseline is Valkey (a Redis fork), not upstream Redis, so baseline_in_list=false. No hardware, compiler or flags are stated. The codebase was written by an AI assistant (Maestro, iGent AI), per the README. The HN submission title 'Outperforms Valkey' overstates the README's own mixed table.

notes: Every number in claimed_speedup matches the README exactly. Cargo.toml declares 'MIT OR Apache-2.0' and the README says the project is dual licensed; GitHub reports only MIT because the repo has a single LICENSE file. The last commit on the default branch (main) is 2025-11-05; the record's 2025-11-28 date is from the non-default branch feature/bit-operations-implementation. The project is still active.

tier_reason: The README has one first-party timing (10.72s vettel vs 13.26s redis for 1000 keys), and the scripts are public (benchmarks/vettel.py, benchmarks/redis.py). make.sh builds vettel without any -O flag (an unoptimized -O0 build), which caps it at C, and the Redis build is unstated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 10.72s (vettel) vs 13.26s (redis) wall time to add 1000 keys, about 1.24x (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: 1000 sequential set commands, each spawned as a separate process from Python os.system: 'vt -c "set k v"' (vettel appends to a flat file) vs 'redis-cli set k v' (TCP round trip to a Redis server), timed with the fish shell's time
corrections.hardware: MacBook Pro (13-inch, Mid 2012), 2.5 GHz Dual-Core Intel Core i5, 16 GB 1600 MHz DDR3, macOS Catalina 10.15.7 (from the README screenshot assets/my_machine.png; the exact i5 SKU is not named)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: vettel: clang -Wall -Wextra -pedantic with no optimization flag (default -O0), per make.sh; Redis/redis-cli build unstated
corrections.caveats: The benchmark measures per-key process spawn: the vt CLI doing a flat-file append vs redis-cli doing a TCP round trip to a Redis server. It does not measure store throughput, so it is not a like-for-like comparison with a Redis server. Vettel is a ~300-line single-file C store with no server. The margin is small (about 1.24x), from a single run, on a 2012 laptop, and vettel itself was built at -O0. Not independently reproduced.

notes: The numbers are on the page, but the 1.24x ratio is derived. The screenshot gives the hardware more precisely than the record did. The comparison is methodologically weak (it is dominated by process startup) but is a real, recognizable Redis comparison, so it is kept at C. The MIT license is confirmed; the last commit is 2023-02-12, so it stays abandoned.

tier_reason: The README and docs/performance.md give first-party ops/s against cachetools and functools.lru_cache, and the benchmark code is public (benchmarks/bench_all.sh, benchmarks/_bench_runner.py). Hardware is given only as 'Apple M-series (arm64)' with no chip model, so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Single-threaded, cache size 256: 20.4M ops/s vs cachetools 826K, about 24.7x (derived from page data; docs/performance.md lists 19.1-27.0x across cache sizes 32-1024). Multi-threaded with the GIL enabled, 16 threads: 19.5M vs cachetools+Lock 795K, about 24.5x (derived from page data). About 1.6x faster than functools.lru_cache+Lock in multi-threaded runs. Plain functools.lru_cache is about 1.5x faster than warp_cache single-threaded (31.0M vs 20.4M ops/s).
corrections.workload: Python @cache() decorator hit/miss throughput (ops/s) on Zipf-distributed keys (2000 unique), cache size 256, median of 3 rounds, CPython 3.13.2. Single-threaded vs lru_cache/cachetools/cachebox/moka_py; multi-threaded (GIL-enabled, 1-32 threads) vs lru_cache+Lock and cachetools+Lock.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust release profile lto="fat", codegen-units=1 (Cargo.toml); CPython 3.13.2 built with Clang 20.1.0 (docs/performance.md); rustc version unstated
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark in the project's own repo, not independently reproduced. The CPU is given only as 'Apple M-series', with no exact model. The stdlib incumbent functools.lru_cache beats warp_cache by about 1.5x single-threaded. warp_cache only wins against lru_cache when a threading.Lock is added (about 1.6x). The ~25x wins are against pure-Python cachetools.

notes: The record's '~26x at 16 threads' is overstated: the page shows 19.5M vs 795K, about 24.5x, and that baseline is cachetools+Lock. The record also left out that stdlib lru_cache is faster single-threaded. The original benchmark_url (/blob/main/) returns 404 because the default branch is master. The last commit on master is 2026-06-18; the record's 2026-08-19 is a push to the non-default branch refactor/benchmark-workflow. The project is still active and the MIT license is confirmed.
